scene1_screen1.text: They were strangers just hours ago — two passengers aboard the same cruise, crossing paths briefly at breakfast and again during the emergency alarms.

scene1_screen2.text: But when the storm hit and the evacuation failed, they ended up in the same life raft. Now, it’s just the two of them. Washed ashore. Alive.

scene1_screen3.text: Waves pound behind them like a threat. Wind cuts across the open sand. The world has narrowed to salt, adrenaline, and each other.

scene1_screen4.text: Nick wipes a cut from his brow. Sofia pushes wet hair from her face, trying to steady her breathing.

scene1_screen6.text: I think so. I don’t know. It all happened so fast… It’s hard to believe we’re even here.

scene1_screen7.text: Same. I thought we were going under for sure.

scene1_screen8.text: I’m Nick, by the way. Travel writer. Mostly survival stories, actually — which feels like a cruel joke right now.

scene1_screen9.text: (managing a breathless smile) Sofia. I’m a marine biologist. Guess I’m finally getting hands-on experience.

scene1_screen10.text: They shake hands — more out of instinct than civility. They're damp, bruised, and scared. But alive.

scene1_screen11.text: At least we didn’t wake up alone. That counts for something.

scene1_screen12.text: Don’t get too comfortable. If rescue isn’t coming soon, we’ll need shelter. Water. Fire. A plan.

scene1_screen13.text: (grinning despite himself) So, no welcome drink? No tiny umbrellas?

scene1_screen14.text: (dry) You picked the wrong cruise package.

scene1_screen15.text: They share a short laugh — thin, uncertain — but it’s the first moment that feels human since the ship cracked in two.

scene1_screen16.text: Before moving from the shoreline, they search what’s left of the raft. They salvage a dented survival kit, a torn blanket, two plastic bottles — one half full, one empty — and a packet of crackers.

scene1_screen18.text: Sofia shades her eyes, scanning the beach. There’s no one else in sight. Just sea. Sand. Trees. And silence.

scene1_screen19.text: There’s some driftwood and palm leaves over there. What do you think — set up here? Or look for better ground?

opts.text: Stay on the beach and start building a shelter here.
Scout inland for a safer, elevated location.
Suggest splitting up to explore faster.

scene1_choice1_option1_screen1.text: Sofia plants her hands on her hips. The sun’s dropping fast, and her legs still tremble from the crash.

scene1_choice1_option1_screen2.text: We’re exposed here, but if a rescue team shows up, they’ll search the coastline first. It’s open, visible. That might be our best shot.

scene1_choice1_option1_screen3.text: So we stay in plain sight. Signal if we see anything?

scene1_choice1_option1_screen4.text: Exactly. Plus, I’m too exhausted to go climbing cliffs right now.

scene1_choice1_option1_screen5.text: They gather broken planks and palm fronds, working together in silence. Between two leaning palms, they fashion a crude shelter. Not safe. But safer.

scene1_choice1_option1_screen6.text: (resting for a second) You give good orders, you know.

scene1_choice1_option1_screen7.text: (sitting beside him) I survive by instinct. And you?

scene1_choice1_option1_screen8.text: I survive because of people like you.

scene1_choice1_option2_screen1.text: Sofia’s gaze tracks the treeline — the dark edge of the unknown.

scene1_choice1_option2_screen2.text: The beach is easy, but it’s also where the waves return. One more storm and we lose everything. Inland might give us protection. Higher ground. Maybe fresh water.

scene1_choice1_option2_screen3.text: (hesitant) Won’t we be harder to find?

scene1_choice1_option2_screen4.text: Only if they’re actually looking. We need to survive long enough to be found — not just wait.

scene1_choice1_option2_screen5.text: They gather what they can carry and move toward the trees. It’s tough going — sand giving way to dense underbrush — but after a short hike, they find a shaded clearing with drier soil and a view of the beach below.

scene1_choice1_option2_screen6.text: This spot... it feels less temporary.

scene1_choice1_option2_screen7.text: It needs to be. Just in case this isn’t a short stay.

scene1_choice1_option3_screen1.text: Sofia eyes the horizon, calculating distance and risk.

scene1_choice1_option3_screen2.text: We don’t have time to explore everything together. If we split up, we might cover more ground before sundown.

scene1_choice1_option3_screen3.text: (shaking his head) No offense, but splitting up is how horror stories start.

scene1_choice1_option3_screen4.text: (level) This isn’t a story. It’s survival.

scene1_choice1_option3_screen5.text: He watches her for a moment. Then sighs.

scene1_choice1_option3_screen6.text: Fine. But we stay within shouting distance. And check in every ten minutes.

scene1_choice1_option3_screen7.text: They part ways down two nearby paths — not far, but not together.

scene1_choice1_option3_screen8.text: Nick’s route curves toward a rocky outcrop. Sofia leads toward the dense jungle.

scene1_choice1_option3_screen9.text: Each step feels heavier than the last.

scene1_screen20.text: Above them, gulls wheel in the darkening sky.

scene1_screen21.text: Below — one beach, two survivors, and no one coming. Not yet.

scene1_screen22.text: But they’ve made a choice. And sometimes, that’s the first step toward not dying.

scene2_screen1.text: They didn’t plan to end the day like this. Shelter half-finished. Bellies half-empty. Hearts completely full of questions

scene2_screen2.text: Nick sets the last driftwood plank into place, brushing dirt from his hands. Sofia kneels by the fire, feeding in kindling. The flames catch, painting her skin in amber.

scene2_screen3.text: For the first time since the wreck, they breathe. Just a little.

scene2_screen4.text: (exhaling) Remind me never to complain about room service again.

scene2_screen5.text: (dryly) Next time, check the cruise forecast before boarding.

scene2_screen6.text: They chuckle — a thin laugh, but real. The air between them has softened, now threaded with shared effort. Shared luck. Shared fear.

scene2_screen7.text: (sitting, thoughtful) You know, I thought I was signing up for a glossy travel article. Photos of sunsets. Notes on fish.

scene2_screen8.text: I thought I was giving a lecture on reef conservation to retirees with daiquiris. Not... this.

scene2_screen9.text: Silence again. But it’s warmer now — not from the fire, but the gravity of being stranded together and still breathing.

scene2_screen10.text: (quietly) I guess it takes a disaster to get people talking.

scene2_screen11.text: (shrugs) We’re out of distractions. And clothes that smell like anything but saltwater.

scene2_screen12.text: Nick laughs softly. Then lies back, folding his arms behind his head. Sofia stretches out beside him, but not too close. Not yet.

scene2_screen13.text: (after a beat) You ever tell the truth in your stories? Or just the version people like better?

scene2_screen14.text: (not defensive — just tired) Both. Depends on how badly I need to believe it.

scene2_choice1.text: What’s something you’ve never told anyone — not even in your books?

opts.text: Give her the truth. Raw and real.
Dodge with a light story — half true, half charm.
Turn it around — not as a game, but to invite her in.

scene2_choice1_option1_screen1.text: Nick doesn’t speak for a while. The fire crackles. Waves roll and retreat. Finally, he sits up.

scene2_choice1_option1_screen2.text: (low) I was supposed to be traveling with someone. My brother.

scene2_choice1_option1_screen3.text: We used to take a trip every year. But this time, he backed out. Said he had work. Said it wasn’t important.

scene2_choice1_option1_screen4.text: Truth is... we haven’t spoken in over a year. Not really. And I think I booked this trip to prove to myself that I didn’t care. But I do.

scene2_choice1_option1_screen5.text: He looks at her now — exposed, not with skin, but soul. Sofia doesn’t fill the silence. She just listens. And that’s more than enough.

scene2_choice1_option1_screen7.text: I’m not sure. But maybe I can fix something.

scene2_choice1_option2_screen1.text: Nick grins, dusts off his pants, and leans in like he’s about to tell a secret to a campfire.

scene2_choice1_option2_screen2.text: I once tried to impress a woman by swimming with sharks in Australia.

scene2_choice1_option2_screen3.text: (arching a brow) Let me guess — didn’t go well?

scene2_choice1_option2_screen4.text: Let's just say I screamed louder than the boat engine. The woman ended up comforting the shark.

scene2_choice1_option2_screen5.text: Sofia laughs. But her eyes search his face. She knows he’s hiding something. But maybe hiding is his only survival skill right now.

scene2_choice1_option3_screen1.text: Nick shifts, lying on his side now. His tone softer. Curious.

scene2_choice1_option3_screen2.text: What about you? What made you get on that boat?

scene2_choice1_option3_screen3.text: (quietly, after a long breath) I needed to see something beautiful again. Something alive. After a year that... wasn’t.

scene2_choice1_option3_screen5.text: Not to death. But it felt like it. A job, a person, a version of myself. I didn’t think I could find her again.

scene2_choice1_option3_screen6.text: Nick doesn’t joke. Doesn’t push. He just watches her. Like she’s the story now.

scene2_choice1_option3_screen7.text: (soft) Maybe this island’s not all bad. It gave me you.

scene2_choice1_option3_screen8.text: She doesn't smile. But she doesn't look away.

scene2_screen15.text: They lie down side by side, the hush between them less like silence, more like peace. Nick shifts closer. Not touching — just near enough to share breath, to let warmth stretch between them.

scene2_screen16.text: Sofia lets her eyes close first. Then Nick. The last thing either hears is the ocean.

scene2_screen17.text: And then — a wind shift. A low rumble beyond the treeline. The storm isn’t done yet.

scene3_screen1.text: The night had started almost peacefully. The fire was out. The shelter stood. They were even laughing a little.

scene3_screen2.text: Then Nick stood up, muttered something about “answering nature’s call,” and disappeared into the darkness near the trees.

scene3_screen3.text: Five minutes passed. Then ten. Then a distant sound — not the waves, not the trees. A sharp, human sound.

scene3_screen6.text: She grabs the flashlight, shaky with worry, and bolts into the night. The wind is picking up — a cold, early warning. Lightning cracks over the sea.

scene3_screen7.text: She finds him slumped near a fallen branch, gripping his leg. Blood seeps through his pants, mixing with sand and mud.

scene3_screen8.text: (urgent, kneeling beside him) Oh god — what happened?

scene3_screen9.text: (grimacing) Slipped. Rock or root. I didn’t see... It’s not deep, just messy.

scene3_screen10.text: (snapping) Messy can still get you killed. Come on. We’re getting you back.

scene3_screen11.text: It takes everything she has. He’s taller, heavier — but he leans on her, limping, one arm over her shoulders — moving back to the shelter.

scene3_screen12.text: Sofia eases him onto the blanket, grabs the first aid pouch, and starts cleaning the wound. Her hands shake, but her focus doesn’t waver.

scene3_screen13.text: (through gritted teeth) You could’ve left me out there. That would've been easier.

scene3_screen14.text: (not looking up) Too bad I’m not into easy.

scene3_screen15.text: She finishes bandaging his leg, tight and efficient. He exhales, resting his head back, breath ragged. Outside, the storm fully hits — deafening wind, horizontal rain.

scene3_screen16.text: They sit close now. Closer than before. With Nick’s leg elevated, Sofia wrapped in the blanket beside him, still catching her breath. The walls shake. The air is electric.

scene3_screen17.text: (quietly) You didn’t have to come looking for me.

scene3_screen18.text: (shrugs) Well, you’re annoying, but I’d rather not be stranded alone.

scene3_screen20.text: The silence between them sharpens. The storm howls — but inside, the quiet feels louder.

scene3_screen22.text: (meeting her eyes) So is everything about this.

scene3_screen23.text: Another long beat. Her gaze lingers on his face. His fingers twitched — close to hers. Every nerve is awake now. The storm outside isn’t the only one crashing down.

scene3_choice1.text: What do you do with this moment?

opts.text: Lean in and kiss him — let the moment take over.
Keep the spark unspoken — focus on survival.
Deflect the tension with a joke.

scene3_choice1_option1_screen1.text: Sofia’s breath catches in her chest. Her body still thrums with adrenaline — but now, it’s not from fear.

scene3_choice1_option1_screen2.text: (low, almost to herself) Screw it. We might not make it through another night.

scene3_choice1_option1_screen3.text: She leans in. He doesn't stop her. Their lips meet in the darkness — fierce, unsure, and painfully real.

scene3_choice1_option1_screen4.text: His hand finds her jaw, steady and warm; hers rests against his chest, feeling the rhythm beneath. The storm outside howls, but inside, it’s quiet — the world narrowed to just the two of them, caught in something neither wants to escape.

scene3_choice1_option1_screen5.text: It’s messy. Salt and heat. But neither pulls away.

scene3_choice1_option2_screen1.text: She swallows hard. Her instincts pull her in two directions — but her mind wins this time.

scene3_choice1_option2_screen2.text: (calmly) Let’s just stay warm. That’s all that matters right now.

scene3_choice1_option2_screen3.text: She adjusts the blanket around them. Her hand rests near his — not touching, but so close it’s almost worse.

scene3_choice1_option2_screen4.text: He nods. Doesn't press. But in the dark, he smiles — like he’s reading something in her silence.

scene3_choice1_option3_screen1.text: (dryly) If you’re trying to seduce me with a bleeding leg and storm sweat, it’s a bold strategy.

scene3_choice1_option3_screen2.text: (grinning faintly) Wasn’t the plan, but if it’s working, I won’t complain.

scene3_choice1_option3_screen3.text: (laughing, gently) Let’s just try not to die tonight. Then you can test your game on me tomorrow.

scene3_choice1_option3_screen4.text: They chuckle quietly. The wind rattles the walls. Her shoulder brushes his — and stays there.

scene3_screen24.text: They lie side by side. Exhausted. Warm. Breathing in unison beneath the thin, half-wet blanket. No more words. Just steady breath. Her hand brushes his. Sleep takes them — finally.

scene3_screen25.text: And when the morning comes, the island will still be there. And so will the hunger. Tomorrow, they’ll have to find food. Water. Answers. But tonight — they survived.

scene4_screen1.text: The morning after the storm is quiet. Unnaturally quiet. Their clothes are still damp. Bellies empty. But Sofia walks ahead with purpose. Nick trails behind — slower today, distracted.

scene4_screen3.text: (grimaces slightly) I’m fine. Just sore. And starving. Mostly starving.

scene4_screen4.text: She doesn’t push him — just keeps walking until the path widens... and they see it. A cave. Hidden behind brush and hanging vines.

scene4_screen5.text: (dry) Is this where you finally eat me?

scene4_screen6.text: (smirking) Not unless you start complaining louder.

scene4_screen7.text: He grins faintly, but there’s something distant in his eyes. As she starts toward the entrance, he hesitates — then follows.

scene4_screen8.text: The cave is deeper than it looks. Inside, it’s cool. Dry. Almost... sacred. But something in Nick shifts. His smile fades. His steps slow.

scene4_screen10.text: (quietly) I used to explore caves like this when I was a kid. Grew up in the Rockies. My brother and I would sneak out and climb into the mountain cracks with flashlights and peanut butter sandwiches.

scene4_screen12.text: One time, we got lost for five hours. Thought we were going to die. My brother started crying. I joked about writing a survival book just in case we made it out.

scene4_screen14.text: (shrugs) Maybe. Or maybe I just wanted to believe that getting lost always meant you’d be found.

scene4_screen15.text: He runs his fingers over the cave wall — but this time, not as a tourist. As if trying to remember who he used to be.

scene4_screen17.text: I’m still trying to figure out what I’m running from.

opts.text: Go deeper into the cave — alone.
Invite Sofia to examine the carvings together.
Sit down with Sofia — and ask for her story instead.

scene4_choice1_option1_screen1.text: Nick takes a deep breath. His hand brushes her shoulder gently.

scene4_choice1_option1_screen2.text: Stay here. I want to check the back — just in case.

scene4_choice1_option1_screen4.text: (firm) I’ll yell if I fall into a pit of doom. Promise.

scene4_choice1_option1_screen5.text: He disappears into the shadows with a flashlight made from a salvaged phone. Minutes pass. Long enough for Sofia to grow anxious — just as his voice echoes back:

scene4_choice1_option1_screen6.text: (excited) Sofia! You need to see this.

scene4_choice1_option1_screen7.text: She rushes to the back — where he stands beside a dusty crate, half-covered in rock. Inside: a broken emergency radio. Heavy. Old. But real.

scene4_choice1_option1_screen8.text: Sofia exhales sharply — a sound between relief and disbelief — and without thinking, she throws her arms around him. His arms catch her, steady and warm, and in that breathless second, their lips meet.

scene4_choice1_option1_screen9.text: It’s not passion. Not hunger. It’s survival — a desperate kiss that tastes like hope, salt, and the first promise that they might just make it out of this alive

scene4_choice1_option1_screen10.text: Someone was here. Someone with tech. If we fix this… we might have a shot.

scene4_choice1_option2_screen2.text: You ever seen markings like these?

scene4_choice1_option2_screen3.text: (approaching) Maybe... Polynesian? No, older. Could be indigenous — maybe even remnants of a shipwrecked crew centuries ago.

scene4_choice1_option2_screen4.text: (lightly) Imagine surviving something like that. Then dying before anyone knows you ever existed.

scene4_choice1_option2_screen5.text: She glances at him. His voice is calm — but his hands are clenched.

scene4_choice1_option2_screen6.text: Hey. That’s not going to be us.

scene4_choice1_option2_screen7.text: Not if I can help it.

scene4_choice1_option2_screen8.text: As they keep exploring, they find an old supply crate — rusted shut. Nick pries it open. Inside: a broken emergency radio, wrapped in canvas.

scene4_choice1_option2_screen9.text: (low) Someone else tried to call for help. Maybe... we still can.

scene4_choice1_option3_screen1.text: Nick sinks to the ground, back against the cool stone.

scene4_choice1_option3_screen2.text: I’ve been talking a lot. Maybe it’s your turn. Who was Sofia before the sea decided to drop her on my beach?

scene4_choice1_option3_screen3.text: (dry) Annoyed marine biologist. Low on grant money. High on caffeine.

scene4_choice1_option3_screen5.text: (quieter) I was supposed to be on that boat with someone. My colleague. He got sick last minute.

scene4_choice1_option3_screen7.text: Yeah. But I’d do it again. Because out here… I feel like I remember what matters. Who I am when no one’s watching.

scene4_choice1_option3_screen9.text: That version of you is kind of incredible.

scene4_choice1_option3_screen10.text: They sit in silence for a moment. Then Nick leans to the side, brushing away moss. His hand knocks into something solid — a half-buried metal box. Inside: a broken radio.

scene4_choice1_option3_screen11.text: (joyful) I think we just found our plot twist.

scene4_screen18.text: The radio is ancient, but the branding is military. A number is scratched into the casing. A call sign?

scene4_screen19.text: (holding it up) If we can fix it... this changes everything.

scene4_screen20.text: (grinning faintly) Guess I’m finally writing a survival story I didn’t make up.

scene4_screen21.text: They emerge from the cave with more than they entered with — not just knowledge, but possibility. A glimmer of connection. A chance.

scene4_screen22.text: Outside, the sun is higher now. But so are the stakes; they finally found hope.

scene5_screen1.text: The walk back is quiet — not strained, just full. Full of everything unsaid, everything survived. The weight of the broken radio sits between them like a fragile hope.

scene5_screen2.text: Nick carries it gently in his arms, like it's made of glass and miracles. Sofia walks a step ahead, her jaw tight, mind spinning. Her pulse hasn't slowed since the cave.

scene5_screen3.text: (glancing over her shoulder) You okay carrying that?

scene5_screen4.text: (soft) I’ve held worse things with more hope.

scene5_screen5.text: They stop where the jungle meets the sand. The sea roars in the distance, gentler now. The wind smells like salt and promise.

scene5_screen6.text: Sofia turns to face him. She watches him with something fragile in her eyes — not fear, not pity. Something else.

scene5_screen7.text: (quietly) Do you think it will work?

scene5_screen8.text: (studying the broken knobs, the frayed wires) I think it’s broken as hell. But broken doesn’t mean useless. If I can fix the transmitter... maybe we have a chance.

scene5_screen9.text: Sofia exhales, her body finally relaxing — not in relief, but in acceptance. At least one problem might be fixable.

scene5_screen10.text: She steps closer, standing so near she can smell the sun on her skin, the faint ozone from the cave dust.

scene5_screen11.text: I don’t know what this place is doing to me. But I haven’t felt this... alive... in a long time.

scene5_screen12.text: (smiling, eyes locked on hers) I haven’t felt anything this real in a long time.

scene5_screen13.text: The tension isn’t sudden — it’s been growing, slowly, steadily, like the tide. And now it crests.

scene5_screen14.text: Sofia reaches for his shirt, half in instinct, half in disbelief. Her fingers barely graze him. He leans down, meeting her halfway.

scene5_screen16.text: She breaks the kiss first — just long enough to breathe. Her eyes glisten, and she rests her forehead against his.

scene5_screen17.text: (whispers) We can’t lose focus. This island might not give us a second chance.

scene5_screen18.text: (softly) Then we make the first one count.

scene5_choice1.text: What do you want to do with this moment?

opts.text: Let the kiss deepen and turn into something more.
Step back to savor the feeling without rushing.
Pull away playfully, tease him to keep things light.

scene5_choice1_option1_screen1.text: She pulls him in again, his breath catches, and her body presses against his like a question that’s already been answered.

scene5_choice1_option1_screen2.text: Clothes are still damp, hands clumsy, but none of it matters. They fall into the sand, laughter caught between kisses and gasps.

scene5_choice1_option1_screen3.text: (against her lips) If this is insanity... I don’t want the cure.

scene5_choice1_option1_screen4.text: (smiling, breathless) Then we’re in this together.

scene5_choice1_option1_screen5.text: The sun sets behind them. And for the first time, they’re not two strangers stuck in survival. They’re something more.

scene5_choice1_option2_screen1.text: She lingers in the moment, then gently presses her palm to his chest. Not rejection. Just pause.

scene5_choice1_option2_screen2.text: (soft) Let’s hold onto this. But not lose ourselves in it. Not yet.

scene5_choice1_option2_screen3.text: Nick nods, grounding himself in the honesty. They sit on the sand, shoulder to shoulder, watching the last of the sun disappear.

scene5_choice1_option3_screen1.text: (grinning, stepping back) You get one kiss for finding a radio. Don’t push your luck.

scene5_choice1_option3_screen2.text: (grinning) One? I was hoping for a subscription model.

scene5_choice1_option3_screen3.text: They laugh, easy and unguarded. But beneath the teasing, something real simmers — a slow burn they’re both starting to feel.

scene5_screen19.text: The moment lingers, even as the sky fades to indigo.

scene5_screen20.text: They return to their shelter, quieter now. But not uncertain.

scene5_screen21.text: (decisive) I’ll scout tomorrow. Look for a better place to shelter — in case the weather turns again.

scene5_screen22.text: (lifting the broken radio) And I’ll see what I can do with this relic. Might take a miracle.

scene5_screen23.text: (smirking) Good thing we’ve already had one.

scene5_screen24.text: They nod to each other, their roles unspoken but set. Partners. Survivors. And tomorrow... maybe something more.

scene6_screen1.text: The applause fades gently. Not roaring, not theatrical — more like respect. The kind reserved for people who’ve survived something that changed them.

scene6_screen2.text: Nick leans slightly forward, hands clasped. He doesn’t smile much — not because he’s unhappy, but because memory still lives close to the surface.

scene6_screen4.text: (softly) Nick Carver. Thank you for being here. Salt and Flame isn’t just a survival memoir. It’s a love story. A human one. But… I’d like to ask Sofia something, if I may.

scene6_screen5.text: Sofia nods once. Calm. Collected. But there’s something in her eyes — not nostalgia, not regret. Just the truth.

scene6_screen6.text: He tells it beautifully. But is it true? That moment — when the sky was collapsing and everything seemed lost… Did you really believe there was a tomorrow?

scene6_screen7.text: (after a long breath) No. I didn’t believe in tomorrow. I believed in him.

scene6_screen8.text: Her voice is quiet, but nothing about it wavers. Nick looks at her — not surprised, just moved. As if her answer still reached something inside him, he thought was long settled.

scene6_screen9.text: He fixed the radio. I don’t know how. He was bleeding, exhausted — we hadn’t eaten properly in days.

scene6_screen10.text: But somehow, he made it spark. And rescue was already searching. That’s what saved us, brought us home. But what changed me was everything before that.

scene6_screen12.text: (turning to Nick) Him. We weren’t lovers on that island. Not at first. We were strangers, then survival partners.

scene6_screen13.text: And somewhere in the middle of storms and silence, I found someone I could trust more than the world I came from.

scene6_screen14.text: He made me laugh. Made me furious. But mostly — he made me feel like I wasn’t alone.

scene6_screen15.text: Nick exhales, not with relief, but with that strange weight that only comes with being seen. Entirely.

scene6_screen16.text: She scared the hell out of me. Because she saw me — not just the version I wrote about. The version I usually run from.

scene6_screen17.text: (leaning back) And now? After everything? You’ve told the world your version, Nick. But Sofia — what’s yours?

scene6_choice1.text: What do you choose to say?

opts.text: We found love there. And I’m still living it.
We shared something extraordinary. And that’s enough.
We’re not what we were — but we’ll always be more than strangers.

scene6_choice1_option1_screen1.text: (softly, smiling) The island was an accident. But he wasn’t. We didn’t plan for each other. But we survived for each other. And we’re still writing that story.

scene6_choice1_option1_screen2.text: Nick reaches for her hand. She lets him. Their fingers interlace. Nothing performative. Just because they want to.

scene6_choice1_option1_screen3.text: Some people come home. I never left — because wherever he is, that’s the place I want to be.

scene6_choice1_option2_screen1.text: (measured, clear) What happened between us was real. But survival changes people. So does peace.

scene6_choice1_option2_screen2.text: She glances at Nick. Their eyes meet — warm, not wistful.

scene6_choice1_option2_screen3.text: We went our separate ways. No drama. No regret. But we still talk. Sometimes with words. Sometimes with silence.

scene6_choice1_option2_screen4.text: I didn’t fall in love with a man. I fell in love with a moment. And I’ll carry it with me. Always.

scene6_choice1_option2_screen5.text: Nick nods, quietly. A truth shared is still a bond.

scene6_choice1_option2_screen6.text: We didn’t fall apart. We just… didn’t hold on. And that’s fine. She’ll always be part of the story I carry.

scene6_choice1_option3_screen1.text: (calmly) We never tried to define it. Not then. Not now. And maybe that’s what made it work.

scene6_choice1_option3_screen2.text: Nick tilts his head slightly, listening. Her voice is not distant — just honest.

scene6_choice1_option3_screen3.text: We weren’t meant to be a perfect ending. We were a story about human connection. Real. Raw. Imperfect. But unforgettable.

scene6_choice1_option3_screen4.text: She smiles at Nick — soft, knowing.

scene6_choice1_option3_screen5.text: She saw the worst in me. And didn’t look away. That’s more than most people ever get.

scene6_choice1_option3_screen6.text: She smiles — soft and knowing. The kind you carry long after someone’s gone.

scene6_choice1_option3_screen7.text: We saved each other. Sometimes that’s all the love you need.

scene6_screen18.text: Two people. Two versions of the same story. But only one truth: even in the most hopeless place, somewhere between salt and flame, they found something worth surviving for.

scene6_screen19.text: What would you like to say to each other after learning about Nick and Sofia's story? Would you be able to trust a stranger on an island?
